question: ap1
prompt:
Constraint: every one of your ideas must be carried out using patient-derived samples. Within that constraint, make the ideas as informative as possible.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Serial-biopsy persistence test across a drug holiday
ideas.description: In patients with planned intermittent dosing (e.g., BRAF/MEK or EGFR inhibitor holidays), collect matched pre-treatment, on-treatment, and off-drug biopsies and profile them by single-nucleus ATAC/RNA multiome to ask whether AP-1 motif accessibility and AP-1 target expression induced on-treatment persist after the stimulus is withdrawn. Persistence that is uncoupled from ongoing MAPK/JNK signaling (measured by phospho-ERK/JNK staining on the same specimens) is the core signature of memory rather than sustained signaling.

ideas.title: Recall kinetics in patient-derived organoids after wash-out and re-challenge
ideas.description: Expose patient-derived organoids to drug or cytokine, wash out and expand for a defined number of divisions, then re-challenge and compare the speed and amplitude of the AP-1-dependent transcriptional response to naive sibling cultures. A faster or larger second response that scales with retained AP-1-primed accessibility distinguishes true memory from simple re-induction.

ideas.title: Clonal barcoding to test heritability of the AP-1 state through division
ideas.description: Lentivirally barcode low-passage patient-derived cells or PDX-derived lines, split each barcoded population into twin arms, and test whether AP-1-high clones in one arm predict AP-1-high or resistant fate in the sister arm. Concordance across sibling clones demonstrates a heritable, clonally transmitted AP-1 state rather than stochastic fluctuation.

ideas.title: Relaxation dynamics after sorting on a live AP-1 reporter
ideas.description: Introduce a TRE-driven fluorescent reporter (or sort on a validated AP-1 surface-marker proxy) into patient-derived organoids or lines, FACS-isolate the top and bottom tails, and track how quickly each fraction re-establishes the parental distribution. Slow, multi-generation relaxation implies a long-lived memory state, whereas rapid re-equilibration implies fast stochastic switching.

ideas.title: Causal necessity and sufficiency via degron and CRISPRa in patient-derived organoids
ideas.description: In patient-derived organoids carrying an auxin-inducible FOS/JUN degron or dCas9-based activation targeted to AP-1-bound enhancers, degrade AP-1 only during the maintenance window after stimulus removal to test whether the stored state is erased, and separately force AP-1 in naive cells to test whether it alone installs the primed state. ATAC and CUT&RUN readouts reveal whether the enhancer landscape is lost, retained, or newly created.
